scope: Proposition 10.7 (Interior visits and nested polygons) of the manuscript “Signed cylinder propagation and marked polygons on the honeycomb lattice” (preprints/Signed-cylinder-propagation-and-marked-polygons-on-the-honeycomb-lattice-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2dda2109318f92bb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 89. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D be a finite convex tessellation polygon and let v be a honeycomb vertex not adjacent to a boundary port. Sum over all ordered first-exit boundary chords of D that visit v, and put SD(v) = X γ∋v xN(γ) cos(3T(γ)/8). Let Zv be the partition of disjoint unoriented cycles in D strictly enclosing v and avoiding it, with cycle weight 2x|λ|. Let Zout(λ) count disjoint cycles in D surrounding and disjoint from λ with the same weights. At a vertex of λ, call the corner convex or reflex when its interior angle is 2π/3 or 4π/3, respectively, and put cλ = (√ 2, v is a convex corner of λ, 2 + √ 2, v is a reflex corner of λ. Then SD(v) = 3Zv + X λ∋v cλx|λ| Zout(λ). (10.14) For each of the three incident face centers f, let ZD(f) be the partition of disjoint cycles in D surrounding f, again with weight 2x|λ|. Put kλ = 1 at a convex corner and kλ = 2 at a reflex corner. Then X f∼v ZD(f) = 3Zv + X λ∋v 2kλx|λ| Zout(λ). (10.15) In particular the ordinary visit mass P γ∋v xN(γ) is comparable, with absolute positive constants, to P f∼v ZD(f).
